properties.name: The undeclared-seam finding can never reach zero: couplings are read from DEPENDS_ON and contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES, and on this design those two sets are disjoint by construction
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 on reflow2's own design (2845 nodes), while starting work on the gap 'x72 pair(s) of parts depend on each other with no contract written down'.

THE NUMBERS:
  component couplings (Component DEPENDS_ON Component)      72
  ...of those, with a two-sided contract                      0
  declared contract pairs (an Interface with both a
    PROVIDES and a CONSUMES side)                            26
  ...of those, carrying a DEPENDS_ON edge                     0

The two sets are COMPLETELY DISJOINT. `seam_sets` computes `couplings` from DEPENDS_ON alone and `declared` from PROVIDES/CONSUMES alone, then subtracts. Since nothing in this design is recorded both ways, the subtraction is a no-op and the finding reports 100% undeclared no matter how many contracts anyone writes. WRITING A CONTRACT DOES NOT CREATE A DEPENDS_ON EDGE, so the number cannot move. This is a list that cannot reach zero, which is the third instance of that pattern found in one day.

THE CAUSE IS A LEVEL SPLIT, AND IT IS VISIBLE IN TWO LINES:
  all 72 coupled pairs are cmp <-> cmp (module level)
  22 of the 26 contract pairs involve a sys: subsystem; only 4 are cmp <-> cmp

So the design records CONTRACTS at the subsystem boundary and DEPENDENCIES at the module boundary, and the detector compares one against the other.

THE 72 ARE NOT SEAMS. Every one of them is INSIDE A SINGLE CRATE - zero cross a crate boundary, measured by mapping each component to its realizing artifacts' paths. And 43 of the 54 files in reflow2-core are `impl DesignGraph`: they are one type split across files for readability, not clients across a contract. Demanding a published contract between two impl blocks of the same struct is an alarm on correct work.

THE REAL BOUNDARIES ARE ALREADY DECLARED, which the finding's wording hides. The four cmp <-> cmp contract pairs are exactly the genuine ones - cmp:service <-> cmp:graph (reflow2-mcp to reflow2-core), cmp:service <-> cmp:registry, cmp:skills <-> cmp:service, cmp:init <-> cmp:export - and every external dependency is specified too (6 of the 17 Interfaces have no provider at all because they are things reflow2 consumes: the dynograph APIs, the ambient agent, the MCP protocol, an authenticating gateway, an exclusive local store).

=> SO THE STANDING READING OF THIS DESIGN WAS WRONG. '0 of 10 subsystems publish a contract - reflow2 specifies everything it depends on and almost nothing it offers' is not what the graph says. It publishes 11 interfaces with providers and consumes 6 it does not own. What it does not do is draw DEPENDS_ON at the boundaries it has published, which is the only reason the seam metric reads zero.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and it is a modelling decision for the owner rather than a defect to repair: which level should carry contracts, and whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is a dependency worth recording at all.
